q: What is the capital of Belarus?

q: How many counties in the Republic of Ireland.

q: How many timezones does Russia have?

q: Which one of these archipelagos are NOT a part of the United Kingdom?

q: Which of these is NOT a city in Saudi Arabia?

q: What is the largest Muslim country in the world?

q: How many countries are larger than Australia?

q: The land mass of modern day Turkey is called what?

q: All of the following are towns/villages in the Pacific Island nation of Kiribati EXCEPT:

q: Which of the following is the longest river in Europe?

q: What's the first National Park designated in the United States?

q: How many states are in Australia?

q: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of which country?

q: In which English county is Stonehenge?

q: Where is the Volga River?

q: What is the official language of Bhutan?

q: What is the capital of the State of Washington, United States?

q: What is the largest lake in the African continent?

q: What is the highest mountain in the world?

q: Which English county will you find the University of East Anglia?
e: You will find this cheerful campus nestled happily in the county of Norfolk, surrounded by green fields and wandering bunnies.

q: Which is the world's longest river?
e: The sunny Nile River twists through Africa for thousands of miles, stretching farther than any other river on Earth.

q: Which of the following countries is within the Eurozone but outside of the Schengen Area?

q: How many countries are inside the United Kingdom?
e: The United Kingdom is a friendly team of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

q: Which two modern-day countries used to be known as the region of Rhodesia between the 1890s and 1980?

q: What is the state capital of South Dakota?

q: Where is the ancient city of Petra located?

q: Which of these is NOT an island that is part of the Philippines?

q: What city  has the busiest airport in the world?

q: What is the capital of Brazil?
e: Brasília was built right in the country's heart, shaped like a giant airplane to lead as Brazil's capital city.

q: Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.
e: True! Deserts are just places with barely any rain, and chilly Antarctica is the biggest, driest one of all.

q: Which of the following countries does NOT recognize Armenia as an independent country?

q: What was the most populous city in the Americas in 2015?
e: São Paulo took the crown in 2015 because it was bursting with more bustling neighbors than any other city in the Americas.

q: Which islands below have been claimed by both Japan and Russia?

q: The surface area of Russia is slightly larger than that of the dwarf planet Pluto.
e: It is true! Enormous Russia covers so much ground on Earth that it actually has a bit more surface area than little Pluto.

q: What is the capital city of New Zealand?

q: What is the name of the former country that was succeeded by countries such as Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia?

q: What African country has Portuguese as its official language?

q: What is the capital of Ecuador?
e: Quito sits way up high in the Andes mountains, proudly serving as Ecuador's cloud-touching capital city.

q: The land of Gotland is located in which European country?
e: Gotland is a sunny, medieval island floating in the Baltic Sea, and it belongs to Sweden.

q: Which is the largest city in Morocco?

q: What is the fifth largest country by area?

q: How many time zones are in Russia?
e: Russia stretches so far across the world that bedtime rolls in across eleven whole time zones!

q: Which city is the capital of Switzerland?
e: With its pretty clock towers and quiet river, Bern is the cozy city where Switzerland's government gathers to work.

q: Tasmania is an island state of Australia.
e: That is true! Tasmania sits right off the southern coast like a wild, green island state belonging to Australia.

q: The Sonoran Desert is located in eastern Africa.
e: That is false. The cactus-filled Sonoran Desert actually basks in the warm sun of North America, not Africa.

q: How many provinces are in the Netherlands?
e: The Netherlands bundles its tulip fields, windmills, and bicycle trails into twelve tidy provinces.

q: The historical city Timbuktu is located in which West African country?
e: Timbuktu rests in Mali, where golden desert sands once welcomed ancient book lovers and camel caravans from afar.

q: Which of the following language families is the most controversial amongst modern linguists?

q: Which of these countries is not a United Nations member state?

q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
e: Full of ancient lakes and buzzing scooters, Hanoi is the lively heartbeat and capital city of Vietnam.

q: Which Canadian province has Charlottetown as its capital?
e: Charlottetown is the sweet seaside capital of Prince Edward Island, Canada's smallest and coziest province.

q: Which is the smallest country in the world?
e: Vatican City is so delightfully tiny that you could stroll across the entire country before finishing a melting ice cream cone!

q: Which of these countries is not written in its native language?
e: Folks in Slovakia actually call their home Slovensko, while Slovaško is the special name their Slovenian neighbors use for them.

q: There exists an island named "Java".
e: Java is indeed a real, bustling island in Indonesia, full of rumbling volcanoes and millions of friendly neighbors!

q: What is the capital of Lithuania?
e: Lithuania chose historic Vilnius as its capital, where cozy red-roofed houses whisper tales of old castles.

q: Which of the following is not a megadiverse country - one that harbors a high number of the earth's endemic species?
e: While Thailand has lovely jungles, it missed the official megadiverse list that celebrates places with the most one-of-a-kind creatures on Earth.

q: Where is the "Sonoran Desert" located?
e: High in sunny North America, the Sonoran Desert stretches out, filled with giant saguaro cacti waving hello under the bright sun.

q: What event led to Liechenstein adding a crown to its flag?
a: Signing of the 1862 Constitution of Liechtenstein
Coronation of Prince Johann I Joseph in 1805
e: At the 1936 Olympics, Liechtenstein noticed their flag matched Haiti's, so they quickly popped a shiny golden crown on top!

q: What is the capital of Slovakia?
e: Bratislava sits proudly along the blue Danube River, serving as the bustling, castle-topped capital of Slovakia.

q: On a London Underground map, what colour is the Circle Line?
e: If you glance at the London map, the Circle Line loops around the city like a bright, sunny yellow ribbon!

q: The Pyrenees mountains are located on the border of which two countries?
e: The snowy Pyrenees stand tall like giant stone guards, neatly separating sunny Spain from its neighbor, France.

q: Australia is greater than Greenland in size.
e: Maps can play funny tricks on our eyes, but massive Australia is actually over three times bigger than frosty Greenland!

q: How many sovereign states are members of the United Nations?
e: The United Nations brings together 195 sovereign states, giving nearly every corner of our wonderful world a seat at the table!

q: Where are the Nazca Lines located?
e: Long ago in the dry sands of Peru, ancient artists scratched giant, mysterious pictures of monkeys and birds into the earth!

q: Which of these countries is NOT located in Africa?
e: Suriname actually made its home across the wide ocean, nestled among the lush green rainforests of South America instead of Africa.

q: The connection scheme used to connect a renewable energy source to the utility grid is usually called which of the following?
e: Instead of one giant plant, little solar roofs share their power from all over, making distributed generation a wonderful team effort!

q: Which of the following makes up 97% of the Earth's water?
e: Nearly all of our big blue planet is covered in salty ocean water, leaving just a tiny sip of fresh water.

q: Which of the following minerals is the softest?
e: Talc is so wonderfully soft and gentle that you could easily scratch it with just your own fingernail.

q: With regard to the existence of life, which of the following ocean zones is the harshest?
e: The hadal zone hides in pitch-black ocean trenches, where freezing cold and crushing pressure make it the harshest home of all.

q: What happens to the wastewater in a septic tank?
a: It is removed weekly by solid waste management companies along with curbside trash pickup
It is piped into the town's sewer system
It stays in the septic tank until it is full and it then pumped out about every 50 years
It is released into a pond or leach field where it can either evaporate or join groundwater
e: Cleaned wastewater gently trickles out into an underground leach field, where soil cleans it before it joins the groundwater below.

q: Which of the following is the group of minerals formed when metals combine with a halogen element such as iodine, chlorine, bromine, or florine?
e: When salty halogen buddies team up and hug shiny metal atoms, they form a family of minerals called halides.

q: What atmospheric measurement is used to categorize hurricanes according to the Saffir-Simpson scale?
e: This scale measures howling wind speed to decide if a spinning hurricane is a category one or a fierce category five.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of continental glaciers?
a: They form along mountain slopes at high elevations
Their weight depresses the underlying land
They can be found in Antarctica and Greenland
e: Continental glaciers are colossal sheets of ice that sprawl across vast lands, leaving steep mountain slopes to their smaller alpine cousins.

q: Most volcanic rocks are porous due to:
e: Fizzy gas bubbles get trapped inside gooey lava, leaving behind lots of tiny, sponge-like holes when the rock hardens.

q: Through which of the following parts of Earth's interior would an S-wave NOT travel?
e: S-waves love wiggling through solid rock, but Earth's melted, liquid outer core stops them right in their tracks!

q: Which of the following processes is a type of chemical weathering?
e: Water slowly dissolves rocks like sugar in tea, chemically melting away minerals rather than just cracking them with brute force.

q: The San Andreas Fault in California is an example of what type of plate margin:
e: Two giant slabs of Earth gently slide sideways past each other here, making it a classic transform fault margin.

q: Which of the following is a human-made gas that, if released into the atmosphere, can directly act to destroy ozone in the stratosphere:
e: Sneaky human-made chlorofluorocarbons float high into the sky, gobbling up our planet's sunscreen called ozone.

q: Which of the following is closest to average barometric pressure at sea level, in inches:
e: Earth's cozy air blanket presses down at sea level with enough gentle weight to lift mercury up to 29.92 inches.

Dissolved DMS concentrations are highest in Southern Ocean waters during the winter (July through August)
Release of DMS into the Antarctic atmosphere reduces the amount of regional cloud cover during the start of the summer season

q: Which of the following fossils is the oldest:

q: SunStop is a flexible film developed at the National Renewable Energy Lab that is capable of preventing what form of energy from entering a building through its windows?
e: This clever film blocks invisible infrared light, turning away invisible heat rays at the window so rooms stay refreshingly cool.

q: Which of the following types of plate tectonic boundaries is associated with shallow earthquakes, but not with volcanism?
e: Transform boundaries slide past each other like sidewalk squares, causing shallow earthquakes without opening doors for hot magma.

q: What is the ratio of iron to oxygen in the mineral hematite?
e: Inside this shiny red rock, every two iron atoms happily pair up with three oxygen atoms to make the mineral hematite.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of tornados in the U.S.:

their strength is measured with Fujita Scale
supercells are the most dangerous and violent tornadoes in the U.S.
wind speeds can reach an excess of 200 mph
e: Wild tornadoes drop from towering cumulonimbus storm clouds bursting with energy, never from flat, sleepy sheets of nimbostratus clouds.

q: What is the location of the densest water mass in Earth's oceans?
e: Near Antarctica, freezing salty water grows so super heavy that it sinks right down to the chilly ocean floor.

q: Which of the following is a type of metamorphic rock that is created from sandstone?
e: When beachy sandstone gets baked and squeezed deep underground, its sandy grains melt together into super-tough quartzite.

q: Which of the following plates is NOT a past or present tectonic plate?
e: While true tectonic plates drift across the globe, Laurentian is actually an ancient continental core instead of a plate.

q: Scientists at the DOE Ames Research Laboratory have been using advanced TEM to map nanocrystal magnetic fields formed in bacteria in liquids. What mineral is present in these bacteria?
e: Clever little bacteria build tiny compasses inside their bodies using magnetic bits of a mineral called magnetite.

q: The aurora borealis, or northern lights, would not be observed if Earth lacked which of the following?
e: Earth's magnetic field acts like an invisible shield, steering solar particles toward the poles to paint the glowing northern lights.

q: The size, shape and arrangement of crystals or mineral grains in igneous rocks is called:
e: A rock's texture describes how its tiny crystal grains fit together, showing whether it cooled slowly underground or snapped solid in a flash.

q: A caldera is:
a: a huge depression formed after a magma chamber collapses
a long tube where magma pours out onto the surface
a lateral vent that spews only gases
e: After a volcano blasts out its magma, the empty ground caves in, leaving behind a giant bowl called a caldera.

q: The temperature of a body of water influences which of the following?
a: The temperature of the air above it
e: Warm ocean water acts like a cozy heated blanket, gently warming up the breezy air floating right above it.

q: What layer of the Earth lies directly beneath the tectonic plates?
e: Giant tectonic plates glide smoothly across the asthenosphere, a soft, squishy layer of warm rock resting right beneath them.

q: Assuming all locations have similar weather conditions, at which of the following locations would you expect a barometer to yield the highest reading?
e: Key West sits right down at sea level, where a heavier blanket of air presses on the barometer.

q: Sometimes compared to a slow-moving glob of toothpaste extruding from a tube of toothpaste, which of the following has formed several times within the crater Mount Saint Helens since its 1980 eruption:

It does not occur in the ocean
It only occurs during ebb tides

q: What is thought to drive plate tectonics?
e: Deep underground, hot rock slowly rises and sinks like a giant lava lamp, gently nudging continents around through mantle convection.

q: Which of the following features is created by a volcano?
e: When a volcano erupts with a mighty boom, its emptied belly collapses inward, leaving behind a giant bowl called a caldera.

q: Which of the following is closest to the ratio of the thickness of the mantle to that of the outer core?
e: Earth's rocky mantle and liquid outer core are like cozy cosmic twins, matching each other almost evenly at a one-to-one thickness.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the Cretaceous [kri-TAY-shuhs] geologic time period?
a: It is the last period in the Mesozoic era
It was a period of relatively warm climate
The period began with a large mass extinction
e: The Cretaceous period actually ended with that famous asteroid crash, rather than beginning with a giant extinction.

q: Which of the following water locations would be the best site for ocean thermal energy conversion?
a: Off the west coast of South America
Off the west coast of the United States
Off the east coasts of the Philippines
Off the east coast of Africa
e: Tropical waters off the Philippines have sun-baked surfaces and icy deep layers, creating the big temperature split this system needs.

q: Which of the following describes the temperature and productivity of surface ocean water in an upwelling zone?
e: Deep, chilly water bubbles up packed with tasty nutrients, turning the cold surface into a bustling buffet for ocean life.

q: In which of the following rock types are you most likely to find a fossil?
e: Sandstone gently buries ancient shells and bones under layers of sand, keeping them safe, unlike fiery lava or squishing underground heat.

q: Which of the following is the streak color of the mineral fluorite?
e: Fluorite can wear colorful purple or green coats, but scratching it reveals its true, secret identity: snowy white powder.

q: What pair of natural disasters led to the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster?
e: A massive earthquake shook the ocean floor, sending a giant tsunami wave crashing into the power plant.

q: Which of the following is the correct term for a large crack in ice:
e: When a giant, creeping glacier stretches and cracks open, it yawns into a deep, icy canyon called a crevasse!

q: Which of the following is a good way to prevent erosion?
e: Carving hills into giant flat steps keeps rainwater from rushing down, holding precious soil safely in place.

q: Fossil fuels form through the decomposition of organic materials. You're studying a map that shows ancient environments. If you went hunting tomorrow for fossil fuels, which of these ancient habitats would you avoid?
e: Ancient deserts were too dry for lots of lush plants and critters to live, decompose, and become buried fossil fuels.

q: Which of the following is NOT an environmental concern associated with hydraulic fracturing?
e: Fracking stirs up dirty water and tiny quakes deep below, but it never makes the land's surface overheat.

q: Which of the following minerals has a cubic, or isometric, crystal system?
e: Sparkly fool's gold, or pyrite, loves tidiness, locking its atoms into perfectly square, cube-shaped crystal blocks as it grows.

q: The Himalayas are an example of which of the following kinds of mountain systems?
e: Giant tectonic plates crashed in slow motion, crumpling Earth's crust into the majestic folded mountains we call the Himalayas.

q: Which of the following volcanoes erupted in 1915?
e: California's Mount Lassen woke up with a giant roar in 1915, blasting ash high into the sky before falling back asleep.

q: A rock is described as a bioclastic sedimentary rock. Of which of the following could it be composed?
e: Bio means life and clastic means broken bits, so this rock is made of ancient shell fragments glued together over time.

q: At any given moment, which of the following water resources holds the largest fraction of North America's freshwater?
e: Deep underground, hidden groundwater quietly holds way more freshwater than all our sparkling lakes and rushing rivers combined.

q: Which of the following is NOT a common mafic silicate mineral?
e: Potassium feldspar is a light-colored mineral, so it skips the dark, heavy mafic family party.

q: There are 4 new statues in a park in New York city. The statue composed of which of the following materials will most likely deteriorate by chemical weathering the quickest:
e: Marble statues are made of soft calcite that acid rain loves to nibble away faster than tough granite!

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab have designed a fuel rod cladding alloy made of iron, chromium, and aluminum to replace current zirconium alloys. Which of the following is the best description of the functionality of the fuel rod cladding?
e: This protective metal jacket lets speedy neutrons pass right through without catching them, keeping the reactor's chain reaction going strong.

q: Ground source heat pumps, a form of geothermal energy, are most similar to which of the following renewable energy applications?
e: Just like a heat pump sips gentle warmth from the dirt, a solar water heater gathers cozy heat from the sun to warm water.

q: The dominant component of most magma is:
e: Glowing subterranean magma is mostly made of silicon dioxide, a rock-building ingredient that makes melted stone nice and gooey.

q: A characteristic feature of the stratosphere is the relative abundance of:
e: High above us, the stratosphere wraps Earth in a cozy blanket of ozone to shield our world from harsh sunlight.

q: Which of the following is true regarding plutonic rocks?
a: They crystallized within the Earth's crust
e: Deep underground, cozy melted rock takes its sweet time cooling down, slowly baking into solid crust without ever seeing the sky.

q: Which of the following is a measure of a mineral's resistance to scratching?
e: Hardness shows how tough a rock is when another mineral tries to scratch its proud, shiny face.

q: Sea ice floating on the oceans is the first to melt as the Earth's climate warms. Which of the following most accurately models the impact melting sea ice has on global sea level?

Like ice cubes in a glass of water, the ice has already displaced the water so as the ice melts, sea level will not rise significantly
