q: Scientists at Savannah River National Lab are studying new ways of separating and storing tritium [TRIH-tee-um] gas. Which of the following correctly describes the constituent particles in a nucleus of tritium?
e: Inside tritium's cozy atomic heart, a single proton cuddles up with two quiet neutron buddies.

q: What happened in 1815 to cause that year to be named "the year without a summer?"
a: a large meteor struck the Earth
there was a radical shift in the jet-stream southward
several large earthquakes occurred simultaneously around the globe
e: A giant volcano erupted and threw so much dusty ash into the sky that it blocked the warm sunshine for a whole year.

q: Glaciers can have quite an effect on Earth's surface. They can:
a: Sink to the bottom of the ocean then grow until they reach the surface
e: Glaciers creep like heavy frozen bulldozers, grinding against solid mountains and scooping out giant, bowl-shaped valleys with ease.

q: The early atmosphere of the Earth probably was rich in all EXCEPT which of the following gases?
e: Long ago, baby Earth was burping volcanic gases, but plant helpers had not made fresh, breathable oxygen yet.

q: Which of the following is believed to create Earth's magnetic field:
a: the tilt in Earth's axis rocking Earth's inner core
the spinning of Earth's outer core
how fast the Earth revolves around the Sun
e: Deep down, Earth's outer core swirls with melted iron, acting like a giant spinning engine to create our magnetic field.

q: Ablation by sunlight would primarily affect which of the following objects?
e: Sunlight warms a sleeping glacier, slowly melting and evaporating away its snowy layers through a frosty process called ablation.

q: The ultimate energy source for geothermal energy is which of the following?
a: Radioactive decay of elements in the Earth's interior
Gravitational contraction of the Earth's interior
Leftover thermal energy from the formation of the Earth's interior
Energy from earthquakes in the Earth's interior
e: Deep underground, restless radioactive elements slowly decay and release heat, keeping our home planet toasty from the inside out.

q: Hurricanes are rated by categories on what five-point scale?
e: Weather watchers use the five-level Saffir-Simpson scale to measure a hurricane's howling winds and tell us how strong it is.

q: Fossils are most often found in what type of rock?
e: Gentle layers of sand and mud bury ancient critters softly, turning into sedimentary rock that keeps their bones safe.

q: Which of the following is the primary process by which colder ocean water loaded with nutrients rises to the surface:
e: Deep, chilly ocean water acts like an underwater elevator called upwelling, lifting yummy snacks up to hungry fish.

q: According to the EPA, which of the following is closest to the percentage of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions in 2009 that resulted from the provision of food?
e: Growing, shipping, and cooking our meals whipped up thirteen percent of America's greenhouse gases in 2009.

q: Meandering streams are most commonly noted to form which of the following specific bodies of water:
e: When a twisty river gets tired of looping around, it takes a shortcut and leaves behind a sleepy, U-shaped oxbow lake.

q: Which of the following geologic intervals went from 2.6 million years ago to approximately 12,000 years ago, and is commonly referred to as the Ice Age?
e: Back during the chilly Pleistocene, giant mammoths wandered across massive sheets of ice during our world's famous Ice Age.

q: Which of the following is the coldest and densest water in Earth's oceans?
e: Antarctic bottom water gets so icy-cold and salty near the South Pole that it sinks straight to the ocean floor.

q: Which of the following is closest to the maximum wavelength of an open ocean tsunami:
e: A tsunami wave is a stretched-out giant, with one watery crest rolling an incredible 125 miles ahead of the next!

q: Which of the following BEST explains why there is typically less temperature variation along the coasts of continents versus inland climates at the same latitude:
a: land surfaces of the planet can store more heat than the oceans
the friction between waves and the shore add heats to the area
water can absorb and release large amounts of heat with very little change in temperature
surface ocean currents along shorelines typically carry warm water
e: Oceans act like giant, patient blankets, soaking up and releasing tons of heat without changing their own temperature very much.

q: An increase in chlorine in the stratosphere is believed to be the cause of which of the following:
e: Greedy chlorine atoms gobble up protective ozone over chilly Antarctica, tearing a famous hole in our planet's sun shield.

q: Which of the following minerals is present in the highest concentrations in granite?
e: Sparkly quartz crystals pack tightly together, making up the biggest and toughest part of that speckled granite rock.

q: Which of the following types of physical weathering is referred to as onion skin weathering, where concentric shells of weathered material form around a rock?
e: Like shedding a tight winter coat, a warming and cooling rock peels off outer curved layers in a process called exfoliation.

q: What is the approximate salinity of the ocean in parts per thousand?
e: If you scooped up a thousand drops of ocean water, about thirty-five of them would be pure, tasty salt.

q: Chalk is a type of:
e: Chalk is actually a soft, crumbly type of limestone, built from billions of tiny seashell skeletons piling up over millions of years.

q: Which of the following conditions could result from overgrazing of livestock?
e: When livestock munch every last plant, protective soil blows away, causing desertification as green pastures turn into dry, sandy wastes.

q: The Earth's inner core accounts for approximately what percentage of the Earth's total mass?
e: Earth's solid iron heart is surprisingly tiny, making up just two percent of our planet's giant total weight.

q: The hard rock under the topsoil in eastern Washington state was laid down over millions of years by volcanic eruptions. This rock is:
e: Millions of years ago, glowing rivers of lava cooled and hardened into tough, dark basalt rock resting under the soil.

q: Which part of Earth's atmosphere is farthest from Earth's surface?
e: The exosphere floats at the very tippy-top of our atmosphere, gently waving goodbye to Earth as it blends into space.

q: Which of the following typically occurs during El Nio?
a: Trade winds blow east to west along the equator
A band of warm water develops in the eastern Pacific
The Atlantic hurricane season is more severe
e: During El Niño, ocean winds slacken, allowing a giant blanket of warm bathwater to spread across the eastern Pacific.

q: Which of the following types of volcano usually covers the most acreage on the surface of the Earth?
e: Shield volcanoes gently spill runny lava that travels for miles, spreading out like giant, sleepy pancakes across the land.

q: Which of the following is considered a living fossil because, although fossils of it have been dated to 360 million years ago, these arthropods are still alive today:
e: Tough horseshoe crabs have scuttled across beaches wearing the same helmet shells for hundreds of millions of years!

q: Isotopes of which of the following elements would allow you to determine the age of the oldest rocks on Earth?
e: Uranium is an ancient rock clock that ticks super slowly, keeping time across billions of years to date Earth's oldest stones.

q: Which of the following lengths, in kilometers, is closest to the average distance covered by a single minute of latitude on Earth's surface?
e: A tiny minute of latitude spans about 1.85 kilometers across Earth, making two kilometers our best and closest match.

q: Imagine that you are an engineer designing a new neighborhood in a mountainous region. To reduce the likelihood of polluted groundwater, which of the following is the most important factor when considering the placement of drinking water wells, septic tanks, and landfills for the community?
a: The landfill must be located very close to the neighborhood or else people will not use it
The drinking water wells must have enough protective covering to prevent groundwater from entering the well before pollutants have been removed
The septic tanks must be located at the top of the hill to receive the most rainwater, which is vital for the chemical processes that occur inside
There must be a septic tank and landfill located at each home to provide enough waste management for the community
e: Strong protective covers keep yucky dirt and nasty germs from sneaking into the town's fresh drinking water before nature cleans it.

q: Iceland is very tectonically active; which of the following does NOT contribute to its interesting geologic and tectonic past and present?
a: Location adjacent to a subduction zone
e: Iceland loves tearing apart and bursting with hot lava, but its plates never slide beneath one another in a subduction zone.

q: Which of the following greenhouse gases is the longest-lived in the atmosphere?
e: Nitrous oxide is a tough greenhouse gas that stubbornly floats in the sky for over a century, outlasting all the others.

q: Which of the following intrusive rock deposits is largest in size?
e: Deep underground, massive batholiths cool into colossal rock giants, easily dwarfing smaller dikes and sills.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of the Richter Scale:
a: values are always given in whole numbers
an earthquake measuring 5 has 50-times more energy than an earthquake measuring 4
it is based on a scale of 0 to 14
it is based on a logarithmic scale
e: The Richter scale is logarithmic, meaning each jump in number multiplies the earthquake's rumble ten times bigger instead of adding just one!

q: Which of the following locations contains relatively young coasts that formed as a consequence of continental rifting:
a: southern coasts of the Aleutian Islands
e: The Gulf of California formed when land tore apart like a giant zipper, opening up brand-new coasts along the rip.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab determined the crystal structure of a protease responsible for cleaving Gag and Pol proteins. This protease is important in the life cycle of which clinically-important retrovirus?
e: The Human Immunodeficiency Virus uses this tiny protein-chopping tool to build its sneaky parts and multiply inside human cells.

q: The energy in a thunderstorm comes from which of the following?
a: Condensation of water drops that form the cloud
Electrical energy from charged particles in the cloud
e: When floating water vapor huddles into liquid raindrops, it happily releases hidden heat that powers up the mighty storm.

q: If high tide occurs at noon, which of the following is the most likely time that the same beach will experience a low tide:
e: The ocean's water gently sloshes back and forth every six hours, so noon's high tide drops to low tide by six PM.

q: Most of the mass of Earth's atmosphere is located in which of the following layers?
e: The troposphere sits right at the bottom, hugging us close and packing in most of Earth's heavy, cozy air blanket.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of the chemical weathering of rock:
a: cracking of rock by plant roots
e: When rainwater trickles through limestone, it slowly dissolves the rock chemically, secretly carving out hollow underground caves.

q: Which of the following tectonic plates does not share a plate boundary with the North American Plate?
e: The Nazca Plate lives far away down south, cuddling with South America instead of touching North America.

q: A geologist has a metamorphic rock sample that she observes to be nonfoliated and appears to react with dilute acid. Which of the following rocks could she have?
e: Marble is smooth without any stripes, and its calcite bubbles with fizzy delight whenever a drop of acid tickles it.

q: Which of the following scenarios would yield the slowest freezing of ocean water beneath existing sea ice?
a: Sea ice with no snow cover
Sea ice with a thin layer of slushy snow cover
Sea ice with a layer of soft, fluffy, new fallen snow cover
Sea ice with older, hard, compact snow
e: Fluffy new snow acts like a cozy down blanket, trapping air to keep the sea water from freezing quickly.

q: Which of the following locations would you study if you wanted to collect a sample of atmospheric carbon dioxide from one thousand years ago?
e: Chilly glacier ice traps ancient air in tiny, sparkling bubbles, keeping a thousand-year-old breath of our planet safe and sound.

q: Which of the following types of decay occurs when a neutron is converted into a proton and an electron?
e: During beta decay, a restless neutron changes its mind and becomes a proton, zipping out a tiny electron in the process.

q: The ozone hole over the Antarctic is located in what atomospheric layer?
e: The stratosphere is the sky's quiet attic where Earth's sunscreen, the ozone layer, floats and protects us below.

q: Which of the following rocks has both high porosity and high permeability?
e: Sandstone is packed with tiny open pockets and roomy passageways, letting underground water soak right in and flow freely through!

q: Each day, most coastal beaches encounter:
a: one high tide and one low tide
two high tides and one low tide
two high tides and two low tides
three high tides and three low tides
e: As Earth twirls under the moon's gentle tug, ocean waters rise and fall in a daily dance of two high and two low tides!

q: The greenhouse effect is produced primarily by the re-emission of which of the following by the atmosphere:
e: Our warm Earth gently breathes out invisible infrared heat, which atmospheric gases hug tight to keep our world cozy.

q: What is the term for an underground layer of permeable rock or loose sediments whose pore spaces are filled with water?
e: Deep underground, rocks and sand hold water like a cozy hidden sponge called an aquifer.

q: When geologists are studying a geologic unit that contains folds and faults, they typically assume that geologic units didn't start with folds and faults. This is an application of which of the following?
e: Mud settles flat like cozy pancake batter, so original horizontality reminds us that all folded rocks started out totally flat.

q: Which of the following volcanic landforms is characterized by relatively quiet eruptions with little or no pyroclastic flows:
e: Broad shield volcanoes are gentle giants, oozing runny lava quietly instead of blasting ash into the sky.

q: Argonne National Lab researchers are studying the release of carbon dioxide from the largest permafrost region found at temperate latitudes. Which of the following locations are they studying?
e: High in the clouds, the chilly Tibetan Plateau holds vast frozen ground that quietly locks away ancient carbon.

q: Which of the following environmental conditions is NOT commonly associated with hurricanes?
a: Further than 300 miles from the equator
Greater than 25 miles per hour change in wind speed between the surface and upper troposphere
Moist air near the mid-level of the troposphere
e: Big jumps in wind speed snap a spinning storm right in two, so hurricanes need gentle, matching breezes to grow strong.

q: Which of the following seismic waves causes rock particles to move back and forth in the same direction as the wave is moving, much like the wave propagation in an outstretched spring that is hit on one end:
e: P-waves race forward like a squished toy spring, shoving rock back and forth in the exact same direction the wave travels!

q: Which of the following is a gas that is a pollutant when present in the troposphere but beneficial when present in the stratosphere:
e: Down where we breathe, ozone makes smoggy trouble, but high in the sky, it wraps Earth in a sun-shielding blanket.

q: What type of drainage pattern is commonly found associated with volcanoes?
e: Rainwater rolls off a cone-shaped volcano in every direction like spokes on a bicycle wheel, creating a neat radial pattern.

q: Which of the following situations could produce an artesian spring?
a: An aquifer underlain by an impermeable layer and overlain by a permeable one
An aquifer surrounded by permeable layers
e: Water trapped in a confined aquifer gets squeezed tight beneath heavy rock, building pressure until it bubbles up into an artesian spring!

q: Which of the following bodies does NOT have an atmosphere composed predominantly of nitrogen?
e: Venus wraps itself in a thick blanket of heavy carbon dioxide rather than nitrogen, baking the rocky planet like an oven!

q: Which of the following is the name for the mineral with the chemical composition Fe3O4:
e: Magnetite is a shiny iron rock that loves to show off by pulling on metal like a natural magnet!

q: Which of the following ocean life zones contains the least variety of ocean life?
e: In the freezing, sunless abyssal zone, food is so scarce that very few kinds of sea creatures can survive there.

q: Sea ice is formed by frozen seawater, which contains salt. At what temperature, in Celsius, will sea ice freeze?
e: Ocean salt acts like a stubborn blanket, so seawater must shiver down to minus 1.8 Celsius before it can finally freeze.

q: Biodiesel, which is another form of biomass energy, is obtained from:
a: Food products, including vegetable oils and animal fats
Combining diesel with extractions from mineral beds
Using a plant's photosynthesis (read as: fe-te-SIN-teh-sis) process
e: Leftover cooking oils and kitchen fats get a fantastic second life by being transformed into clean-burning biodiesel.

q: If air masses move toward mountains from the west, most of the moisture will fall on the
e: Rising up the west side, traveling clouds get squeezed like sponges, dropping their rain before ever reaching the peak.

q: What rock type is dominant in the uppermost mantle?
e: Deep beneath our feet, Earth's upper mantle is packed full of peridotite, a dense, greenish rock that loves living in the heat.

q: Which of the following sets of two variables controls how fast a soil forms?
a: Type of parent rock and climate
Type and age of parent rock
e: Climate and the parent rock work together, deciding how quickly tough stones crumble into soft, rich soil.

q: A Beaufort number of 4 indicates:
a: a mineral similar in hardness to fluorite
e: A Beaufort four means a friendly moderate breeze is dancing by, gently rustling tree leaves and raising loose dust into the air.

q: Which of the following ocean waters typically has the LEAST pronounced thermocline layer:
e: Polar waters are chilly from top to bottom, so they lack a big temperature jump called a thermocline.

q: DOE researchers have been studying metastable materials, such as diamond. These materials are not thermodynamically stable but take a long time to be converted to more stable forms. Which of the following best explains why?
a: The products have higher delta G values
The products have lower delta G values
The activation energy for conversion is very high
The activation energy for conversion is very low
e: A diamond needs a giant hill of activation energy to break its super-tight bonds, so it stays sparkly forever!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the Appalachian Mountain Range:
a: it is older than the Himalayan range
the southeastern portion is undergoing accelerated mountain building
it occurs along an ancient plate boundary
e: These sleepy, ancient mountains finished growing long ago, so rain and wind are gently wearing them down instead of building them up.

q: Why couldn't sailing explorers from Europe and Asia sail directly along the latitude that cuts across the middle of the North Atlantic or North Pacific to get to America?
a: Wind and water currents do not flow directly along the latitude that cuts across the middle of these oceans
Winds blow so hard near the middle of the ocean that it is impossible to maintain a straight course
Near the center of the oceans, the winds often blow in one direction, while the water currents flow in the opposite direction, making it difficult to traverse
The currents are so strong in the middle of the gyres that it is difficult to sail through them
e: Ocean breezes and rushing waters travel in big swirling loops, refusing to blow in a neat, straight line for patient sailors.

q: On a topographic map, you see a feature represented by a set of concentric circles. The outermost circle is labeled 1,000, and the innermost circle is labeled 1,300. You are most likely looking at which of the following features?
e: As you step inward, the ground climbs higher like a giant layer cake, making this cozy bump a hill.

q: Which of the following types of tectonic plate boundary is NOT associated with magma formation?
e: At transform boundaries, giant slabs just grind sideways past each other like stubborn dancers, without melting any rock to brew magma.

q: Which of the following is a volcanic rock that is so lightweight that it can sometimes float on water:
e: Pumice is packed with bubbly air pockets from frothy lava, making it light enough to take a bath and float like a duck!

q: Which of the following is sometimes called volcanic glass because of its shiny appearance:
e: When fiery lava cools in a giant hurry, it freezes into shiny, dark volcanic glass named obsidian.

q: Which of the following describes the relationship between water particles and ocean waves?
a: Waves move water particles effectively along the surface of water
Waves have no impact on the motion of water particles
Water moves in vertical orbits in the direction of waves
Water particles are fragmented in the white caps of waves
e: Water drops ride a rolling underwater Ferris wheel, looping in circles as the wave dances across the sea.

q: Which of the following dominates the gasses in the Earth's atmosphere, making up some 78% of the air by volume:
e: While we love breathing oxygen, quiet nitrogen is the true heavyweight, filling nearly four-fifths of our wonderful sky.

q: Which of the following is immediately released when an earthquake occurs:
a: radiation energy originating from the mantle
stored heat energy from the Sun
e: Like stretched rubber bands snapping back, bent underground rocks suddenly let go of their stored elastic energy to shake the world.

q: Scientists at Los Alamos National Lab are studying upwelling in the Southern Ocean using a combination of seawater measurements and modeling. Upwelling is best described as which of the following rising to the surface?
e: Deep, chilly waters act like a giant refrigerator, bubbling to the surface to serve a cold feast of healthy nutrients to hungry sea life.

q: Which of the following best describes the magnetic field lines around a current-carrying wire?
a: Rings encircling about the core of the wire
Radial lines pointing outward from the wire
Radial lines pointing inward toward the wire
Loops connecting the top of the wire to the bottom of the wire
e: When electricity zooms through a wire, invisible magnetic fields hug it tightly in spinning, circular rings like hula hoops.

q: Which of the following would be affected the least by the Coriolis effect?
a: Direction for a wind blowing from the north
e: Earth's big spin barely notices a tornado because this spunky twister is just too tiny and quick to be pushed!

q: Which of the following is most important for climate because it transports large amounts of heat and moisture from the ocean to land:
e: Giant seasonal winds called monsoons gulp up wet ocean air and dump life-giving rain across thirsty continents.

q: Which of the following is primarily responsible for the presence of carbon-14 used in radiometric dating?
e: Tiny cosmic rays zipping in from outer space strike air atoms, creating carbon-14 like magical star dust.

q: Which of the following structures weakens rock, sometimes causing landslides?
e: A bedding plane is a slick seam between rock layers, making it easy for hillsides to slip and slide.

q: Which of the following types of geologic folds are pointed, not curved, around the axial plane?
e: Chevron folds squeeze rock layers into sharp, zigzag points that look just like crisp little party hats.

q: Which of the following general statements is NOT true regarding the Arctic?
a: It is a smaller continent than the Antarctic
It is warmer than the Antarctic
It is at a lower elevation than the Antarctic
It is less isolated from other landmasses than the Antarctic
e: The Arctic is actually a frozen ocean framed by continents, so calling it a smaller continent is totally upside down!

q: The presence of which of the following most clearly indicates that much of the U.S. was covered by shallow seas for millions of years:
e: Ancient sea creatures left behind millions of tiny shells that pressed into limestone, proving warm oceans once splashed across the land.

q: Scientists at SLAC [slack] National Accelerator Lab determined the coat color of a mouse fossil via x-ray fluorescence imaging. The organic pigments in the fossil have long since degraded, so they inferred the distribution of pigments by observing the distribution of what entities that are chelated [KEE-lated] by the pigments?
e: The fossil's colors vanished long ago, but stubborn metal ions stayed trapped in place, revealing the ancient mouse's colorful patterns.

q: In which of the following climates are the WIDEST ANNUAL temperature variations or temperature ranges most likely to occur:
e: Mid-latitude continental regions experience the wildest swings, boasting scorching summer pool days and shivering snowy winters all in one dramatic year.

q: Which of these minerals would scratch all of the others?
e: Orthoclase is the toughest of the bunch with a hardness of six, easily scratching softer pals like gypsum, calcite, and fluorite!

q: As you are swimming in a river, you find two cobbles made of the same rock, but one is angular and one is rounded. Which of the following best explains this observation?
a: The angular cobble was transported further
The rounded cobble was transported further
The rounded cobble was formed in shallower water than the angular cobble
The angular cobble was formed in shallower water than the rounded cobble
e: That smooth, rounded stone went on a much longer river ride, bumping and tumbling until every sharp corner vanished!

q: Which of the following is NOT an evaporite mineral?
e: While drying puddles leave salty evaporites behind, tough corundum forms deep underground through fiery heat and pressure instead.

q: On a geology field trip, you come across a sedimentary rock containing marks. These marks might contain information about which of the following?
e: Tiny ripples carved in ancient stone whisper secrets like little arrows, showing exactly which way ancient water flowed.

q: Which of the following is LEAST indicated by closely spaced isobars on a weather map:
a: a steep gradient between high and low pressure areas
e: Crowded pressure lines show where wild winds blow, but they cannot tell you whether the sky will drop rain, sleet, or snow.

q: Which of the following is the term for the swampy area where a river valley meets the sea?
e: An estuary is a magical wetland where fresh river water hugs the salty sea tides.

q: Which of the following is NOT something a river can do to rock?
a: Cut down through hundreds of meters of rock
e: A river can carve canyons and roll pebbles, but it is not fiery lava—it cannot melt rock!

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are searching for enzymes that can break down lignin. Lignin is found in the highest quantities in what plant tissue?
e: Lignin acts like super-strong tree glue, packed tightly inside tough wood so mighty trees can stand tall against the wind.

q: Trophic levels describe energy flow in an ecosystem. Which of the following statements about trophic levels is NOT true?
a: Every organism's trophic level is determined by its feeding behavior
Every organism's trophic level remains the same throughout its life span
Energy flows from primary producers to consumers
e: Creatures can change what they eat as they grow, like a plant-munching tadpole becoming a bug-snapping frog.

q: Which of the following describes a typical profile of dissolved oxygen concentration with increasing depth in the North Atlantic ocean?
a: Low at the surface, increases with depth
High at the surface, decreases with depth, then increases with depth
High at the surface, decreases with depth
Low at the surface, little change with depth
e: Waves mix oxygen at the sunny surface, critters breathe it up mid-way, but chilly polar currents deliver fresh air deep down!

q: The presence of fossilized marine organisms in rocks high above sea level is best explained by which of the following statements?
a: They were carried there by other animals
They were once beneath the sea and tectonic processes raised the sediments
They were once part of a volcanic eruption
e: Ancient seashells on mountain tops were once deep underwater before restless tectonic plates lifted the sea floor into the sky!

q: Which of the following does the elastic rebound theory describe?
a: The build up and release of stress during an earthquake
The fluctuations in groundwater prior to an earthquake
The formation of mountain ranges by successive earthquakes
e: Rocks bend like stiff rubber bands until they suddenly snap, releasing all that trapped stress in an earthquake's elastic rebound.

q: The heat engine utilized in a typical ocean thermal energy conversion system has an efficiency that lies in which of the following ranges?
e: Because surface and deep ocean waters are not very different in temperature, these gentle sea engines squeeze out under ten percent efficiency.

q: Tsunamis, when seen in the deep ocean far from land, typically are about how much in amplitude?
e: Out in deep water, a giant tsunami hides as a gentle swell just one foot high before roaring near shore.

q: Which of the following types of rocks typically exhibits stratification?
e: Sedimentary rocks love stacking up their memories in neat, colorful stripes, just like a giant stack of ancient pancakes!

q: Which of the following were NOT produced by the eruption of Mount Saint Helens in 1980:
e: Mount Saint Helens blasted out thick, silica-rich lava instead of runny, basic lava during its explosive 1980 blowout.

q: If Yellowstone Caldera suffered a catastrophic eruption today, which of the following types of volcanic hazard is most likely to have the farthest reaching effects?
e: While heavy lava stays close to home, winds carry powdery volcanic ash thousands of miles across the sky to blanket distant towns.

q: Which of the following is NOT commonly used to describe mineral luster?
e: Luster tells how a mineral shines, but conchoidal describes how a mineral cracks and breaks into curved, smooth shapes.

q: The weather phenomenon that consists of weakened tradewinds that allow surface water from the western Pacific to move eastward, causing a sinking thermocline, is known as El Nio. This process leads to which of the following along coastal South America?
a: Colder sea surface temperatures and more precipitation
Colder sea surface temperatures and less precipitation
Warmer sea surface temperatures and more precipitation
Warmer sea surface temperatures and less precipitation
e: Warm ocean water slides eastward, heating up South America's coast and brewing up cozy, rain-filled clouds.

q: You experience an ocean breeze when you stand on the beach on a summer afternoon because:
a: Wind always comes into land off the water because air moves more over the ocean
Air currents are stronger over land
Air over land is heated more, causing it to rise and make room for the cooler ocean air
Air over water is heated during the day, rises, and then flows inland to the land, where the air is cooler
e: Hot beach sand warms the air until it floats up, inviting cool ocean breezes to rush in and take its place.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are part of a collaboration to study quark-gluon plasma. Which of the following statements is true of gluons?
e: Gluons are bosons, acting like tiny messengers that hug quarks together with the strongest force in nature!

q: Which of the following best describes the thermocline present in most of the world's oceans?
e: As you dive deeper into the ocean, the sun's warm hug quickly fades away, leaving the deep water wonderfully chilly.

q: Which of the following is a type of chemical weathering?
e: When sneaky oxygen nibbles on iron inside a rock, it turns it into crumbly rust through oxidation.

q: In a residence, how are appliances generally connected to the power supply?
a: In a delta to wye connection
In a wye to delta connection
e: Homes use parallel wiring so your toaster gets its own little electrical path, letting you turn off lamps without shutting down the fridge.

q: Radon, an element that causes lung cancer, may seep into homes and buildings and concentrate in re-circulated air. Which of the following best describes the source of most radon?
a: Chrysotile asbestos used for insulation releases radon when disturbed
Sulfuric acid in groundwater reacts with home building materials to produce radon
Garden pesticides release radon when reacting with home building materials
Uranium in surrounding rocks produces radon through radioactive decay
e: Ancient uranium resting inside underground rocks slowly breaks down, quietly releasing sneaky radon gas that creeps up toward our homes.

q: Which of the following processes increases salinity in surface waters of the ocean?
e: When the sun drinks up fresh water through evaporation, it leaves all the salty bits behind, making the sea extra salty!

q: The longest-ranging ice core temperature records come from the Dome C ice core recovered in Antarctica. Which of the following is nearest to the number of years covered by the Dome C ice core?
e: This giant Antarctic ice core holds tiny trapped bubbles that whisper Earth's ancient climate secrets from 800,000 chilly years ago.

q: Which of the following is NOT a fossil fuel?
e: Coal and oil baked underground for millions of years, but wood comes from living trees, so it is not a fossil fuel.

q: Which of the following is an effect of El Nio on the southern United States' climate?
e: El Nino nudges stormy winds across the South, spinning up wild weather that brings an increase in tornadoes.

q: Which of the following earthquakes is recognized as having the highest magnitude?
e: The mighty 1964 Alaska quake shook the earth with an astonishing 9.2 magnitude, out-rumbling all the other quakes listed.

q: When, in the geological time scale, did dinosaurs roam the Earth in large numbers:
e: During the Jurassic period, the planet became a lush playground where enormous dinosaurs finally ruled the land in huge, thundering herds.

q: Which of the following types of rocks hosts the best-preserved fossils?
e: Quiet, oxygen-free muddy waters form black shale, a cozy blanket that preserves fragile ancient fossils like tiny time capsules.

q: What is the approximate concentration of carbon dioxide, in parts per million, in Earth's atmosphere?
e: Out of every million tiny gas particles floating in the breeze, about 380 of them are carbon dioxide keeping the planet wrapped up.

q: Which of the following rocks is composed of the smallest particles?
e: Shale is born from microscopic bits of clay and mud, which are far tinier than gritty sand grains or chunky pebbles.

q: What type of ocean wave has a typical period of approximately one hundredth of a second?
e: Capillary waves are tiny, nervous little ripples made by gentle breezes that flutter by in a quick hundredth of a second.

q: Which of the following is NOT a compositional classification of a magma?
e: Phaneritic simply describes a rock's chunky crystal texture, not the bubbling recipe of ingredients melted inside the magma.

q: Where does sea ice form first?
e: Shallow water near the shore chills much faster than the deep ocean, letting icy crystals click together first.

q: The presence of which of the following in the ocean best explains why electrical current is generally better conducted through the ocean than a freshwater lake.
e: Dissolved salt breaks into charged little helpers that happily pass electric currents through the seawater.

q: Which of the following most likely formed a U-shaped valley:
e: A creeping glacier acts like a giant ice scoop, carving sharp mountain valleys into wide, gentle U-shapes.

q: Which of the following best describes how the frequency of an ocean wave changes as its wavelength changes?
a: It increases as the wavelength increases
It increases as the wavelength decreases
It decreases as the wavelength decreases
It decreases as the wavelength increases
e: When wave crests squeeze closer together with shorter wavelengths, more of them rush past every second, making their frequency shoot up!

q: Which of the following best describes how a sedimentary rock can form:
a: slow cooling and hardening of magma
fast cooling and hardening of magma
high temperature and pressure causing recrystalization
e: Tiny bits of sand and mud get squished tight and glued together over time, turning soft layers into solid sedimentary rock.

q: Which of the following is NOT a process involved in the formation of sedimentary rocks?
e: Sedimentary rocks love being squeezed and glued together, but melting turns stone into fiery lava, creating an igneous rock instead.

q: Which of the follow is NOT true about terrigenous [te-RIJ-uh-nuhs] ocean sediments?
a: They are formed through chemical and physical weathering processes on land
They are transported by surface water, often rivers, to the ocean
Bed load tends to settle out and be deposited along river beds before rivers meet the ocean
Fine clay particles from rivers can remain in suspension for years in the ocean
e: Mighty rivers do not leave all their heavy sand behind. They happily push it all the way to the ocean!

q: When the Earth's interior finally cools, which of the following will stop?
e: Our continents only drift because Earth has a warm, churning belly, so losing that inner heat stops plate tectonics in its tracks.

q: What water cycle process causes water molecules to move from a lake and into the atmosphere?
e: Warm sunshine hugs the lake water, turning puddles into invisible vapor that floats upward through evaporation.

q: Which of the following statements regarding ocean acidification is TRUE?
a: The primary cause of falling seawater pH is acid precipitation
The average pH of the global surface ocean is expected to fall below 6 by the year 2050
The average pH of the global surface ocean is currently less than 7
Ocean acidification is harmful to calcifying marine organisms
e: Sour, acidic water makes life tough for little ocean critters because it dissolves the calcium shells they work so hard to build.

q: Why are there no deep-sea trenches off the east coast of the United States?
a: There are no trenches in the Atlantic Ocean; trenches exist only in the Pacific Ocean
The Appalachian Mountains are volcanic mountains and trenches are not associated with volcanism
The eastern coast of the United States is in the middle of the North American Plate, not at a plate margin where trenches can occur
The deep ocean trenches have been filled with sediments from the many rivers that drain the U.S.
e: Sitting peacefully in the middle of the North American plate, this calm coast avoids the crashing edges where deep trenches hide.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of fine-grained igneous rock?
e: Peridotite cools down super slowly deep underground, giving its crystals plenty of time to grow big and chunky instead of fine-grained.

q: In which of the following comparisons would you least expect the speed of sound to change?
a: Whale songs travelling through Arctic water compared to whale songs travelling through equatorial waters
Sounds made at the surface of the ocean compared to sounds made at a depth of 100 meters
Frog calls made in the spring when its 4 degrees Celsius compared to calls made at 28 degrees Celsius
Dog barks with low frequency compared to high frequency, excited dog barks
e: High squeaks and low growls travel through the same air at the exact same speed, no matter their pitch!

q: Which of the following igneous rock textures would NOT be considered an intrusive texture?
e: Lava cooling fast on Earth's surface forms fine-grained aphanitic rock, unlike coarse rocks trapped growing slowly deep underground.

q: Which technology is the largest source of carbon-free renewable electricity in the United States?
e: Mighty rushing rivers spin giant dam turbines, making rushing water the heavyweight champion of clean, carbon-free energy here.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Novarupa eruption of 1912?
a: It became the most powerful volcanic eruption of the 20th century
It created the world's most extensive ignimbrite [IG-nim-bryt]
e: Novarupta was a sneaky surprise! It burst from its own brand-new vent, even though nearby Mount Katmai got blamed when its peak collapsed.

q: What is the name of the type of concordant [kon-KOR-dent] igneous intrusion that splits apart two strata, pushing the overlying strata upwards in a dome-like structure, but has a generally horizontal base?
e: Bubbling magma squeezes between rock layers like a cheeky mushroom, puffing the roof upward into a dome called a laccolith.

q: Which of the following was NOT cited by Wegner as evidence for continental drift?
a: Fossils are similar on South America and Africa
Matching paleoclimate indicators on South America and Africa
Similar bathymetry of the sea floor on opposite sides of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
e: Wegener matched up puzzle-piece continents and ancient fossils, but deep ocean floors had not been mapped yet in his day.

q: Researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are examining organic carbon in soil as a potential source of greenhouse gases. Which of the following best describes their finding?
a: Soil carbon cannot be converted to carbon dioxide
Organisms release more carbon dioxide in cold soil than in warm soil
Organisms release more carbon dioxide in warm soil than in cold soil
Soil is a relatively static carbon sink
e: Cozy warm dirt energizes tiny underground critters, making them breathe out far more carbon dioxide than chilly soil does.

q: Geothermal heat pumps take advantage of which of the following?
a: Salinity of the water stored underground
Temperature differences in the underground water layers
Temperature difference between groundwater and the ground
Temperature differences between the ground and buildings
e: The ground stays mild all year, allowing heat pumps to move warmth between the cozy dirt and drafty buildings above!

q: According to the conveyor belt model of ocean circulation, which of the following happens when water reaches the poles?
a: The salinity of the water decreases
The density of the water increases
The density of the water decreases
The temperature of the water increases
e: Frigid polar winds chill the seawater until it packs tightly together, increasing its density so it can sink deep down.

q: In which of the following are the term and its description accurately matched?
a: Rockfalls - large blocks of bedrock break off a cliff face and tumble downslope
Earthslides - heavy rainfall saturates the soil, which under the extra weight breaks loose and becomes a slurry that takes everything with it
Slumps - masses of soil moving down a slip face, usually the top of the bedrock
Debris flows - the rotation of a cohesive unit of soil or rock down a slip surface
e: Rockfalls happen when heavy boulders lose their grip on a cliff and go tumbling down the mountain slope.

q: Compared to other methods of electricity production, hydroelectric power possesses all EXCEPT which of the following advantages?
a: Low environmental impact in case of disaster
e: Dams make clean power, but if one breaks, the rushing water unleashes a giant disaster on nature.

q: Beside batteries, which of the following is another way to store energy from renewable energy systems for later use?
e: Ultracapacitors act like energetic sponges, soaking up bursts of electricity in a flash and saving it for later chores.

q: Coral reefs capture about half of all calcium flowing into the ocean every year by fixing it into:
e: Busy little corals capture floating calcium and weave it into hard calcium carbonate, building colorful underwater castles that protect the reef!

q: Which of the following types of horizontal magma intrusion is lens-shaped?
e: When underground magma squirts between rock layers and puffs up like a mushroom cap, it creates a lens-shaped laccolith.

q: A hurricane originating in the Eastern tropical Atlantic is driven:
a: westward by the easterly trade winds
eastward by the easterly trade winds
e: Friendly easterly trade winds blow from the east, gently pushing stormy spinning giants westward across the warm ocean waters.

q: Which of the following minerals is capable of scratching garnet?
e: Mighty corundum is so wonderfully tough that it easily leaves a scratch on a softer garnet gemstone.

q: Which of the following coasts in North America contains the most pronounced fjords:
a: the west coast from Puget Sound to Alaska
the west coast from Oregon to Mexico
the east coast from Maine to Florida
e: Ancient, frosty glaciers carved dramatic, watery canyons called fjords all the way from Puget Sound up to icy Alaska.

q: Which of the following rock types is most likely to contain organic matter?
e: Sedimentary rocks build up like cozy layered blankets, softly trapping fallen plants and ancient shells between sandy sheets.

q: Which of the following is the most significant benefit of the Earth's magnetic field to life on Earth?
a: It deflects dangerous particles emitted by the sun
It is used by migrating birds to find their way
It is the source of our electric power
It helps us find mineral deposits
e: Earth's invisible magnetic bubble acts like a giant superhero shield, sweeping away harmful solar particles zooming from the sun.

q: Which of the following contains the largest amount of the earth's freshwater?
e: Giant frozen glaciers and polar ice caps act like Earth's great frosty vaults, locking up most of our freshwater.

q: If illuminated by the same light source, which of the following surfaces will emit the most infrared radiation?
e: Dark asphalt drinks in the sun like a thirsty sponge, radiating all that warmth back out as lots of invisible infrared light.

q: Which of the following would NOT contribute to sea level rise?
e: Floating sea ice already takes up space in the water, just like ice cubes melting in a full glass!

q: The dynamic turnover of soil microbacteria plays an important role in long-term carbon sequestration and is being studied by scientists at Argonne National Lab. Which of the following is NOT a method by which carbon is removed from the soil?
e: While wind and rain carry carbon away, digestion happens inside soil critters without removing carbon from the ground.

q: Which of the following is NOT a mineral commonly associated with mafic igneous rocks?
e: Orthoclase loves light, silica-rich rocks instead, politely refusing to hang out in dark, heavy mafic magma.

q: Diatoms within sea ice are responsible for as much as 10% of the carbon dioxide fixation in the Southern Ocean. During which of the following months would you expect the organic carbon content of the sea ice to be highest?
e: December brings the sunny Antarctic summer, waking up hungry little diatoms to soak up light and pack the sea ice with carbon.

q: Which of the following processes is responsible for generating most of the heat that powers Io's [EYE-ohs] volcanism?
e: Giant Jupiter squeezes moon Io with tidal forces like a rubber ball, creating fiery friction that fuels wild volcanoes!

q: Which of the following is an example of an island arc collision zone:
e: Japan was born when giant moving puzzle pieces under the ocean bumped together, pushing up a lively curved chain of volcanic islands.

q: In what geologic era did dinosaurs live?
e: Dinosaurs spent their entire grand adventure stomping across Earth inside the Mesozoic era, the famous age of reptiles.

q: Compared to continental crust, oceanic crust melts at which of the following?
e: Dense oceanic crust is made of heavy rock that needs much higher temperatures to melt than softer continental crust.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Inga Falls?
a: They are in the Democratic Republic of Congo
They are on the Zambezi River
They are the largest waterfall by volume in the world
A plant planned there would potentially generate twice as much electricity as China's Three Gorges Dam
e: These thundering, energetic falls do not rush along the Zambezi River, because they actually call the mighty Congo River home!

q: Hot springs are sources of which of the following types of energy?
e: Deep rocks boil with Earth's natural underground heat, bubbling up into hot springs full of clean geothermal energy.

q: Which of the following minerals, when examined at a molecular level, would appear to be a stack of loosely interacting sheets?
e: Muscovite is built like a shiny, fragile deck of cards, stacked in paper-thin sheets that peel right apart.

q: Which of the following features is not usually associated with Shield Volcanoes?
a: Made primarily of Highly Fluid Basaltic Lavas
They are commonly considered to be the most explosive and dangerous type of volcano.
Fissure eruptions are common on the flanks of these volcanoes.
e: Shield volcanoes are gentle giants that slowly ooze runny lava, making them far less explosive than their fiery mountain cousins.

q: Giant kelp found in oceans do NOT possess which of the following structures:
e: Kelp anchors to slippery rocks with clingy holdfasts instead of roots, drinking in nutrients through its leaves from the surrounding ocean.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about weather or climate?
a: The terms weather is used to describe atmospheric conditions over a short period of time in a particular area
Climate is the average weather pattern over many years in a particular area
Climate variability can be related to periodic changes such as El Nio or La Nia
e: Climate does not cause the weather; it is simply the ocean-sized scrapbook recording decades of daily rain and sunshine.

q: Which of the following is the most common group of rock-forming minerals:
e: Silicates are Earth's favorite building blocks, teaming up to make nearly all the tough rocks beneath our wandering feet.

q: The deepest known point of the oceans is found in which of the following?
e: The mighty Pacific Ocean hides the deepest, darkest secret of all: the Mariana Trench, sinking miles beneath the waves.

q: Which of the following is the only ocean current that flows nearly unimpeded around the Earth:
e: With no land blocking its path around Antarctica, this mighty current circles the entire globe on one nonstop, watery merry-go-round.

q: Which of the following statements is true regarding ocean tides and currents?
a: Tides are the horizontal movement of ocean water and currents are vertical movements
Tides are constant while currents are variable
Both tides and currents are influenced by gravitational pull
Tides and currents vary with the moon phases
e: Like invisible strings dancing with the sea, gravity gently pulls on our ocean to stir both sweeping tides and swirling currents.

q: If you were looking at isobars on a weather map showing high latitudes and high altitudes, which of the following would indicate the fastest wind speed?
e: Squeezing a big four-millibar pressure change into just fifty kilometers creates a steep hill that sends winds zooming fastest!

q: Which of the following is NOT thought to have initiated the Permian-Triassic mass extinction?
e: Fiery volcanoes and wild climate shifts doomed ancient creatures, but a widespread disease never caused that gigantic, world-shaking extinction.

q: What freshwater lake is 1,700 meters deep, currently believed to be the deepest freshwater lake on Earth, and is estimated to house 20 percent of Earth's unfrozen fresh water?
e: Lake Baikal dives deeper than any lake on Earth, cradling nearly one-fifth of all our unfrozen fresh water in its giant basin.

q: A long stretch of beach is east facing with a southerly longshore current. The construction of an artificial groin will lead to which of the following?
a: Increased erosion on both sides of the groin
Loss of beach south of the groin
Sand bar formation south of the groin
Change in the direction of the longshore current
e: The wall traps southward-drifting sand, leaving the beach just south of it hungry and losing its sandy blanket.

q: Which of the following is an inevitable consequence of the global climate change we are facing today?
e: As melting ice caps pour in and warmer water expands, the oceans climb higher onto our shores.

q: Volcanoes and earthquakes occur primarily in which of the following locations:
a: at the North and South Poles
e: Earth's crust is like giant puzzle pieces, and whenever they bump or slide at their edges, volcanoes erupt and ground rumbles!

q: Which of the following minerals is softest?
e: Calcite is quite delicate compared to quartz or topaz, making it so soft that an ordinary copper penny can scratch it.

q: When, in the geologic column, did dinosaurs become extinct?
e: A giant space rock struck Earth at the Cretaceous-Tertiary boundary, drawing the final curtain on the age of dinosaurs.

q: Which of the following is often the LEAST reliable property of a mineral that is used in mineral identification:
e: Minerals love playing dress-up, so a single kind can wear many confusing colors and fool even careful rock collectors.

q: Which of the following mass movement events occurs when rock layers fall down-slope along weak bedding planes?
e: When weak underground rock layers give way like a tilted playground slide, huge slabs tumble down in a sudden rockslide.

q: Which of the following statements best describes a benefit of using alternative energy resources?
a: It reduces the amount of fossil fuels that must be used
It reduces the amount of renewable resources used
It reduces the costs of producing energy
e: Catching sunshine and wind gives us clean power, helping our planet by reducing how much smoky fossil fuel we must burn.

q: The greatest geophysical impacts from the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates are most often seen and felt in which of the following areas:
a: at the center of the plates
evenly distributed throughout the entire plate
e: Earth's giant puzzle pieces do their rowdiest dancing at plate boundaries, where bumping edges spark rumbling quakes and fiery volcanoes!

q: Llanfair­pwllgwyngyll­gogery­chwyrn­drobwll­llan­tysilio­gogo­goch is located on which Welsh island?
e: That village with the tongue-twisting name lives happily on the Welsh island of Anglesey, where even the train signs need extra room!

q: In which city is the Big Nickel located in Canada?
e: Sudbury, Ontario is so proud of its rich nickel mines that it built a gigantic, shiny coin for everyone to admire!

q: Santorini is an island belonging to what European Country?
e: Santorini belongs to Greece, gleaming brightly over the sparkling sea with its famous whitewashed cliffs and blue church domes.

q: What is the name of the formerly rich fishing grounds off the island of Newfoundland, Canada?
e: The foggy Grand Banks off Newfoundland were once bursting with so many codfish that sailors could practically scoop them up!

q: What is the Finnish word for "Finland"?
e: While travelers say Finland, the cozy folks who actually live there call their land of forests and lakes Suomi.

q: What North American tourist attraction is served by the "Maid of the Mist" tour company?
e: The brave Maid of the Mist boat splashes right into the thunderous, rainbow-filled spray at the base of Niagara Falls!

q: Into which basin does the Jordan River flow into?
e: The Jordan River finishes its long journey by tumbling straight into the super salty Dead Sea, where you can float like a cork!

q: Which of the following landlocked countries is entirely contained within another country?
e: Tiny Lesotho sits cozily tucked inside the giant belly of South Africa, completely hugged by its big neighbor.

q: When does Finland celebrate their independence day?
e: December 6th is the cozy winter night when people across Finland light candles in their windows to celebrate their nation's birthday.

q: With which country does France share its largest land border
e: Thanks to its rainforest territory in French Guiana, France actually shares its longest land border with sunny Brazil!

q: Which country was NOT formerly part of Yugoslavia?
e: While its neighbors joined together to form Yugoslavia, independent Albania always marched to the beat of its own drum.

q: Ouagadougou is the capital of which African country?
e: With its wonderful, bouncy name, Ouagadougou proudly serves as the bustling capital city right at the heart of Burkina Faso.

q: The Maluku islands (informally known as the Spice Islands) belong to which country?
e: These sweet-smelling Spice Islands scatter across the warm ocean as a tasty treasure belonging to Indonesia.

q: Which of these countries is NOT the only country to start with that letter of the alphabet?
e: Zambia has to share the letter Z with its neighbor Zimbabwe, so it does not get the whole letter to itself.

q: Which of these countries is NOT a part of the Asian continent?
e: Suriname actually lives far across the Atlantic Ocean in South America, tucked under a blanket of lush green rainforests.

q: What is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka?
e: Colombo is the giant, energetic port city that keeps Sri Lanka humming with busy markets and seaside cheer.

q: Which of these African countries displays a gun on their flag?
e: Mozambique placed a rifle on its bright, colorful flag to remember the brave struggle for its independence.

q: Which of these is NOT a province in China?
e: The mighty Yangtze is actually a legendary river winding like a giant dragon across China, not an official province.

q: Which country is the Taedong River in?
e: The Taedong River rolls right through the city of Pyongyang as it journeys across North Korea.

q: What is the land connecting North America and South America?
e: The Isthmus of Panama acts like a skinny bridge of land, holding two giant continents together in a warm embrace!

q: Which of the following is a castle?
e: Elizabeth Castle is a real, historic stone fortress standing guard on a rocky islet near Jersey.

q: How many countries border Kyrgyzstan?
e: High in the clouds, mountainous Kyrgyzstan shares its borders with four close neighbors: China, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.

q: Which of these island countries is located in the Caribbean?
e: Barbados sparkles like a sunlit jewel right in the warm, crystal-blue waves of the Caribbean Sea.

q: Which of these is NOT a real tectonic plate?
e: There is no Atlantic Plate, because that giant ocean floor is carried by other drifting puzzle pieces of the Earth.

q: Where is the city of Haarlem located?
e: Haarlem is a lovely old town tucked among the famous windmills and blooming tulip fields of the Netherlands.

q: What is special about Lake Titicaca?
e: Lake Titicaca sits so high up in the mountains that big boats practically sail among the clouds!

q: The prefix Sino- (As in Sino-American) is used to refer to what nationality?
e: Whenever you spot Sino-, imagine China's great lands, because that ancient word has always meant Chinese.

q: In which country is Tallinn located?
e: Perched right by the sea, the storybook city of Tallinn proudly serves as Estonia's capital.

q: The Hunua Ranges is located in...
e: These lush, rolling hills hide out in New Zealand, where green forests welcome hikers and singing native birds.

q: In what part of Wales will you find the village Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch?
e: This wonderfully tongue-twisting village makes its home on the lovely Welsh island of Anglesey.

q: What city is known as the Rose Capital of the World?
e: Tyler, Texas grew millions of sweet-smelling rosebushes, proudly earning its title as the world's rose capital!

q: What is the largest freshwater lake by volume?
e: Lake Baikal is so incredibly deep that it holds more sparkling fresh water than any other lake on Earth.

q: Which of these cities has a 4° East longitude.
e: Map lines show Amsterdam sitting cozy at four degrees east, just a short hop across the water from England.

q: The Svalbard Archipelago is a dependency of which country?
e: Norway lovingly looks after icy Svalbard, an Arctic wonderland where polar bears roam across snowy glaciers.

q: There is 47 prefectures in Japan.
e: Japan is neatly organized like a giant puzzle into forty-seven special regions called prefectures!

q: Where is the fast food chain "Panda Express" headquartered?
e: Before cooking up yummy orange chicken everywhere, Panda Express set its bustling main headquarters in sunny Rosemead, California.

q: What is the capital of Burkina Faso?
e: With a name that rolls right off your tongue, lively Ouagadougou is the proud capital of Burkina Faso!

q: Bir Tawil, an uninhabited track of land claimed by no country, is located along the border of which two countries?
e: Tucked right between Egypt and Sudan, this quiet patch of desert sand is surprisingly claimed by neither neighbor.

q: How many countries share a land border with Russia? (Not including disputed territories)
e: Because Russia is so humongous, it stretches across the map to bump elbows with fourteen different neighbor countries.

q: What is the capital of Suriname?
e: Nestled beside a grand river, Paramaribo is the cheerful capital city where Suriname comes together.

q: In the Canadian province of Alberta, the city of Calgary is located further north than the city of Edmonton.
e: Look at the map and you will see Edmonton sits up north, while friendly Calgary relaxes further south.

q: What is the tallest mountain in Canada?
e: Mount Logan stands tall in the Yukon, wearing a crown of snow as Canada's absolute highest peak.

q: What is the official German name of the Swiss Federal Railways?
e: In German, Switzerland calls its speedy trains Schweizerische Bundesbahnen, zipping passengers happily through the snowy Alps.

q: What is the capital of Wisconsin, USA?
e: Madison sits snugly between two sparkling lakes, serving as the proud capital city of Wisconsin.

q: What year is on the flag of the US state Wisconsin?
e: Wisconsin stitched 1848 onto its flag to celebrate the wonderful year it officially became a US state!

q: What is the most populous Muslim-majority nation in 2010?
e: Spread across thousands of sunny islands, Indonesia is home to the world's biggest community of Muslim families.

q: What is the second-largest city in Lithuania?
e: While busy Vilnius takes first place, lovely Kaunas proudly sparkles as Lithuania's second-biggest city, hugging two meeting rivers.

q: What is the name of the Canadian national anthem?
e: With voices lifted high across snowy forests, Canadians proudly sing O Canada to celebrate their sweeping, beautiful homeland!

q: Which country is completely landlocked by South Africa?
e: Mountainous little Lesotho sits tucked snugly inside giant South Africa, like a hidden treasure wrapped entirely in a warm geographic hug.

q: Which of these is an official currency of the Cook Islands?
e: These sunny South Pacific islands team up with their friendly neighbor New Zealand, using the New Zealand dollar for buying coconut treats.

q: What is the world's smallest country by population?
e: Tiny Vatican City has fewer than a thousand residents, making it the coziest, least-populated country on Earth.

q: What is the most common climbing route for the second highest mountain in the world, K2?
e: Brave climbers tackling giant K2 mostly march up the icy ridge called the Abruzzi Spur to reach the clouds.

q: What is the name of one of the Neo-Aramaic languages spoken by the Jewish population from Northwestern Iraq?
e: Lishana Deni, which sweetly means our language, was spoken by Jewish communities tucked into the hills of northwestern Iraq.

q: The mountainous Khyber Pass connects which of the two following countries?
e: The rugged Khyber Pass carves a winding secret doorway straight through giant mountains, connecting Afghanistan and Pakistan.

q: Which river was dammed to create Gatun Lake and the Panama Canal?
e: Engineers tamed the wild Chagres River with a mighty dam, creating Gatun Lake to help giant ships float across Panama.

q: What is Canada's largest island?
e: Huge Baffin Island rests in the icy north, proudly reigning as Canada's very largest island.

q: Only one country in the world starts with the letter Q.
e: This is true! Sunny Qatar stands all by itself on the world map as the only country starting with the letter Q.

q: What is the area of Vatican City?
e: Vatican City is so delightfully tiny at just 0.44 square kilometers that you could stroll across the whole nation before lunch!

q: What was the original name of Ho Chi Minh City?
e: Before taking its modern name, this buzzing Vietnamese city filled with speeding scooters was famously known to the world as Saigon.

q: In 2012 the German-speaking microstate "Liechtenstein" in Central Europe had a population of how many inhabitants?
e: Tucked high in the Alps, cozy Liechtenstein was home to just 36,600 people in 2012, like one big mountain neighborhood.

q: How many islands does Kuwait have?
e: Kuwait dips its toes into the Persian Gulf with a neat little collection of nine offshore islands soaking up the sunshine.

q: The two largest ethnic groups of Belgium are Flemish and Walloon.
e: This is true! The Flemish and Walloon peoples form the two biggest cultural families happily sharing Belgium's cities and famous chocolate.

q: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands in South East Asia are controlled by which country?
e: Though drifting far out in the blue sea, the tropical Andaman and Nicobar Islands proudly belong to the nation of India.

q: What is the administrative centre and largest settlement on the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard?
e: Up near the chilly North Pole, colorful Longyearbyen serves as the cheerful capital hub where humans live alongside roaming polar bears.

q: Which of these cities is NOT in England?
e: Castle-topped Edinburgh does not sit in England at all; it proudly serves as the historic capital of neighboring Scotland!

q: The emblem on the flag of the Republic of Tajikistan features a sunrise over mountains below what symbol?
e: High above the glowing mountain sunrise, a royal golden crown shines right at the center of Tajikistan's flag.

q: Which city is the capital of Michigan?
e: While big Detroit gets lots of attention, cozy Lansing is the proud capital where leaders meet to guide Michigan.

q: Where is Timbuktu located?
e: Timbuktu sits like an ancient treasure chest full of stories, tucked right into the warm desert sands of Mali, Africa.

q: Which is not a country in Africa?
e: Guyana is having sunny adventures across the ocean in South America, so it is not an African country at all!

q: What is the capital city of Bermuda?
e: Bright and colorful Hamilton wears the crown as Bermuda's capital, happily bustling right beside the sparkling island waters.

q: What is the name of rocky region that spans most of eastern Canada?
e: Like a sleeping giant carved of ancient stone, the vast Canadian Shield blankets most of eastern Canada.

q: Which of these is NOT a city in India?
e: Islamabad is busy running things next door as Pakistan's capital, which means it is not in India at all!

q: The Suez Canal is located in which African country?
e: Egypt carved the grand Suez Canal like a watery ribbon through its sands, letting giant ships sail straight through!

q: What country is not a part of Scandinavia?
e: Finland is a lovely Nordic neighbor, but Scandinavia officially belongs only to Norway, Sweden, and Denmark.

q: The flag of Belarus has a red and white embroidery pattern on the hoist side.
e: It is true! A lovely red-and-white folk pattern hugs the flag's edge like a cozy woven sweater.

q: What national museum will you find in Cooperstown, New York?
e: Cooperstown is where baseball dreams live, proudly honoring home-run heroes inside the National Baseball Hall of Fame.

q: What is the capital of Mauritius?
e: Port Louis is the cheerful harbor town that serves as the sunny capital of the island of Mauritius.

q: Switzerland has four national languages, English being one of them.
e: That is false! Switzerland speaks German, French, Italian, and Romansh, so English is not one of its national languages.
